item.title: ISS cricket experiment found microgravity-exposed larvae hatched earlier than ground controls
item.description: In 2005, scientists examined cricket reproduction on the International Space Station, where embryos grew under microgravity conditions. Interestingly, larvae emerged sooner than those on Earth, suggesting that microgravity affects developmental speed while preserving key neural structures. This research is vital for comprehending how life forms adjust to lesser gravitational forces, expanding our knowledge of development beyond Earth. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Freezing liquid inside optical fibre makes light and sound interact 1,000 times more strongly
item.description: Scientists have frozen the liquid inside a special optical fibre to -196°C, creating conditions where light and sound interact more than 1,000 times more strongly than in ordinary fibres. The team found that the frozen fibre could still guide light and hypersonic sound waves. The breakthrough also helped researchers demonstrate optoacoustic memory, which could have potential applications in lower-energy photonic computing, quantum information processing and high-precision sensing. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
